title: Knott's pulls T-shirt after criticism
summary:
By Jacob Sundstrom: Knott�s Berry Farm has pulled a T-shirt promoting its new Knott's Scary Farm haunted house �Inked� following concerns the shirt included a racist caricature. A spokesperson for the theme park did not directly address those concerns, instead saying:

�We are committed to fostering a respectful and inclusive environment for all. We are aware of concerns regarding a T-shirt design associated with a new haunted maze. While it was never our intention for the design to be perceived as offensive, we understand those concerns and regret any offense it may have caused. The shirt has been removed from inventory.�

That reads a little more, �sorry you were offended� and less, �sorry we tried to sell you something offensive.� But it�s undoubtedly good news the T-shirt is no longer on sale. Late last week, Knott�s shared a video highlighting its creative process in a way that seemed to be an effort to quell concerns about the use of generative AI at its Halloween event.

I asked for additional information on the creative process for bringing the drawings you see in the video into the digital plane. I also asked if artificial intelligence is used at all during that process. Here�s the response I received:

�We have a robust in-house design team at Knott's Berry Farm. �Our practice is to create original art. The designers may use digital design and illustration tools, but our policy restricts full use of AI.�

I don�t find the phrase �full use of AI� particularly satisfying, but the spokesperson also provided the following statement about Six Flags� use of artificial intelligence in merchandise creation.

�Authenticity, originality, and respect for creative work are fundamental to Six Flags' creative development process. Our merchandise creative is developed in partnership with professional artists and designers, and our standard practice is to create original work through a human-led design process. We recognize that sophisticated design and illustration tools can sometimes lead to misconceptions about how creative assets are produced; however, originality and artistic integrity remain central to our approach.

�We are committed to supporting the professional artists and designers whose talent and creativity help shape our brand and create memorable experiences for our guests.�

That is, notably, not a denial that artificial intelligence is used during the design process. That�s not a huge surprise; I assume AI is used somewhere in the process for merchandise design at Six Flags. But the when and the how of its use remains very opaque. I do want to focus on one part of that statement:

�We recognize that sophisticated design and illustration tools can sometimes lead to misconceptions about how creative assets are produced; however, originality and artistic integrity remain central to our approach.�

I want to acknowledge that I don�t think engaging in an online witch hunt about every piece of suspicious artwork is a terribly productive use of time. It�s challenging to know definitively whether or not art has been produced by AI except in the sloppiest of use cases.

That�s why it would be great if corporations like Six Flags chose to be more transparent about the ways they�re using AI. Instead, it seems many companies want to hold onto a bit of plausible deniability.

I imagine that�s why the statement stops short of apologizing for selling a T-shirt that, in my opinion, featured a racist caricature. I�m glad the T-shirt was pulled and I�m glad Knott�s chose to engage with us rather than hope the whole thing would blow over. But this won�t erase the suspicion and doubt that has crept into the minds of the fans who love this event.

And unless we start seeing a whole lot more transparency, I don�t imagine that�ll change any time soon.

title: Universal sets opening date for Hollywood Drift
summary:
By Robert Niles: Universal Studios Hollywood's new Fast & Furious roller coaster has its official opening date.

Fast & Furious Hollywood Drift has been in technical rehearsals and previews for the past month, but the coaster will open officially to all park visitors starting September 16.

In case you were wondering, autumn starts on September 22 this year, so Universal juuust made that promised "summer" opening.

The first-of-its-kind Intamin coaster features trains of four cars styles as street racers from the Fast film franchise. Each car spins in a programmed maneuvers to simulate drifting in a high-speed street race. And this one takes place on the Universal City hillside overlooking California's San Fernando Valley.

That setting has created a bit of a problem for the coaster, as local residents complained about its noise during testing. That led Universal to install even more sound barriers around the ride. That work should be completed in time for the official ride debut.

With a top speed of 72 mph, this will be Universal's fastest roller coaster in the world. A second installation of Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift is now under construction at Universal Studios Florida in Orlando. That one will feature and different track design and is looking at an opening sometime next spring, according to our sources. No official opening for that one, yet.

title: Step back in time to visit Universal Studios in 1974
summary:
By Robert Niles: After several years of looking through USB drives, I finally found my family's old home movies of theme park visits from my childhood.

These are silent movies recorded on a Super 8 film camera, which was the latest in home video technology at the time. Years later, my father transferred the Super 8 film to video and then to digital by recording a projection of the films. So do not expect today's HD quality from these videos.

Also, because these were recorded on film - and you only had a limited amount of film on each reel - people tended to shoot short, to conserve that film. The idea was not to document a moment like a professional historian but to capture enough of a moment to help you remember it later.

And remember this visit, I do. The highlight for me was being selected as an audience volunteer to board a San Francisco-style cable car on one of Universal soundstages for a fake Rice-a-Roni commercial that was filmed as part of the Studio Tour experience. Back then, riders exited the "Glamor Tram" to walk through several demonstrations in the soundstages. On this video, you can see the commercial shoot, as well as a makeup demonstration, and a couple of other special effects demonstrations - one in what I remember as a lawyer's office (was it Perry Mason's?) and another in a monster's castle.

And yes, that's me as the last kid off the cable car.

Other scenes on the driving portion of the Tour in this video include 1974's new Runaway Train and the Burning House that had debuted the previous year along with the Parting of the Red Sea. You also can see 1971's Submarine set, as well as the one encounter that remains today on the tour, the Flash Food, which debuted in 1968.

The video also includes scenes on a playground, and while I remember the oversized bench and props being at Universal, I do not remember the conventional playground equipment.

Later this week, I will post my family's home movies from Disneyland, which includes my first visit to the park. I also have home movies from Busch Gardens in Tampa, back when it was called "The Dark Continent," as well as what I think might be video of Busch Gardens Los Angeles.

title: Disney Adventure adds its first port of call
summary:
By Robert Niles: It looks like the Disney Adventure is going someplace... finally.

The Disney Cruise Line's latest ship, Disney Adventure, started sailing from Singapore last spring. Disney's first cruise ship to be based in Asia has not called on any other ports in the region, however. The ship has sailed only "cruises to nowhere" in its maiden season.

That is about to change, though. Disney has announced that Disney Adventure will be adding its first port of call to its itineraries, starting this New Year's Eve. Disney Adventure will sail to Langkawi, Malaysia on select four-night cruises from Singapore in 2027.

Port Adventures available on these itineraries will include Langkawi Highlights with a cable car ride, Island Hopping boat tours including an eagle-watching experience, Kilim Kayak Adventure on the Kubang Badak River, and Colors & Crafts with a Batik-making workshop.

Fares will start at US$1,509 for two people in an inside stateroom. Pearl Castaway Club members may book now, with bookings opening over the next few days by club level. Bookings open to the public on September 8. For assistance in planning a Disney Cruise Line vacation, please contact our travel agent for a free, no-obligation vacation quote.

title: Rope Drop: Happy birthday to Tokyo DisneySea
summary:
By Robert Niles: As the "rope drop" starts a day at theme parks, the Sunday "Rope Drop" post kicks off the week here at Theme Park Insider. Here is what lies ahead for fans at the parks over the next seven days.

Happy birthday this week to Tokyo DisneySea, which celebrates its 25th anniversary on Friday. The Tokyo Disney Resort's second gate opened officially on September 4, 2001 and welcomed more than 12 million visitors in 2024, making it the world's seventh-most visited theme park.

We have a couple of big announcements coming up this week for theme park fans. On Wednesday, Dollywood will announce its plans to honor its late Dreamer-in-Chief, Dolly Parton, who passed away from cancer last week. The next day, on September 3, Six Flags Magic Mountain has promoted that it will make an announcement about its new coaster for 2027, which planning documents revealed would be the first installation of the new Vekoma Thrill Glider model.

Also on Thursday, Halloween Horror Nights opens at Universal Studios Hollywood. In case you missed it, here is my coverage from Universal Orlando's 35th HHN, the Infernal Carnival of Nightmares, including walk-through video highlights from all 10 houses. The Hollywood installation will have eight houses, including the same five IP themes as Orlando's.

Next weekend is the Labor Day holiday weekend in the United States, which makes the traditional end of the summer vacation season. However, that season practically ended in early August as schools reopened for the fall. But parks are keeping the party going with Halloween events opening throughout the month, followed by the return of holiday events at many parks.

Planning a trip?

Here are the current refurbishment schedules from Disneyland, Walt Disney World and Universal Orlando.

September 8: Indiana Jones Adventure closes at Disneyland, with no reopening date.
September 8-11: Mark Twain Riverboat closes at Disneyland.
September 14: Mad Tea Party closes at Disneyland, with no reopening date.
September 14-16: Tom Sawyer Island closes at Disneyland.
September 15-20: The Untrainable Dragon closes at Universal Epic Universe.
September 21-24: Sailing Ship Columbia closes at Disneyland.
October 26: Volcano Bay closes for the season, with a planned return on or before April 1, 2027.
November 20: Jurassic Park River Adventure reopens at Islands of Adventure.
January 4 - February 2, 2027: Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges closes at Islands of Adventure.
January 25 - February 4, 2027: Fyre Drill closes at Universal Epic Universe.
February 8-19, 2027: Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey closes at Islands of Adventure.
Universal's Horror Make-Up Show is closed at Universal Studios Florida. Estimated reopening in winter 2026.
Carousel of Progress is closed at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom. New show debuts in 2027.

title: Walk Time: Turning around a rough week for theme park fans
summary:
By Robert Niles: Halloween Horror Nights has started at Universal Orlando, which is the good news in what was a rough week for many theme park fans.

Things do not look good for the future of the X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain. To be fair, that's because the recent past has been a problem for that coaster and too many of its riders. Multiple reports of brain injuries and at least one death have led to lawsuits, settlements and a state investigation that has kept the Arrow 4D coaster closed for more than a month. Has Six Flags' X2 made its final run?

Down the road at Knott's Berry Farm, the park appears to have stepped in it with what appears to be an AI-designed T-shirt. But generative AI does not seem to be intelligent enough to know that one should not use a Sambo caricature on said merch. Knott's Scary Farm shirt appears to show racist caricature

The big blow this week was the death of Dolly Parton, the music legend and humanitarian whose Dollywood theme park is now among the most-visited in America. Dolly Parton passes away at age 80

  • Theme Park Insider Podcast, Ep. 13: Thank you Dolly

Turning toward the future - and better news, one hopes, Report: Universal Studios Japan plans major expansion.

In Europe, Saudi money is behind a $7 billion Manga Theme Park(s) Coming to Paris.

And back in the Americas, Mexico's 'Luxury Theme Park' sets opening preview date.

Meanwhile, Disneyland starts construction on new parking garage and Walt Disney World sets opening date for Lakeshore Lodge.

The former Six Flags St. Louis, one of the chain's original-build parks, is now Mid America Adventure. Six Flags Fiesta Texas also broke ground on its new Werewolf Gorge family roller coaster while Holiday World has started laying track for its new Mack rides water roller coaster. Construction update: Six Flags, Holiday World start on 2027

On our Discussion Forum, one reader posted, I hope D'Amaro puts the "Animal" back in "Animal Kingdom", while another warns of The coming drought in Orlando theme park development.

Finally, for those of us who track such things, let's dive into what counts as a credit in Did I actually Visit that State?.

Thank you for reading, and I wish you all a wonderful weekend.

title: Smoke and Stack take on Jack at Halloween Horror Nights
summary:
By Robert Niles: For the first time, a major category Oscar-winning film has inspired a haunted house at Universal Orlando's Halloween Horror Nights. Sinners might lead the big names at this year's 35th anniversary haunt event. But once again, it's Universal's original concept houses that steal the show.

Ryan Coogler's "Sinners" won Academy Awards this year for Best Original Screenplay for Coogler, Best Original Score, Best Actor for Michael B. Jordan, and - breaking one of Hollywood's final glass ceilings - Best Cinematography for Autumn Durald Arkapaw, the first woman to win that award. Universal here presents a book-report retelling of the story for its haunted house, starting with our arrival at the Mississippi train station on our way to the opening night party at Smoke and Stack's juke joint.

It's an handsomely presented house, highlighted by that first music scene in the juke joint. But as impressive as the visuals in the house might be, they just can't measure up to an attentive filmgoer's memory of Arkapaw's amazing cinematography or the twists and symbolism in Coogler's clever script. If you've not seen Sinners, perhaps Universal's house will inspire you to give the film a watch. It should. But fans of the film, while delighted with the chance to step into Smoke and Stack's world, likely will leave a bit frustrated by this abbreviated visit.

Beyond Sinners, Universal's next most popular IP house this year might be Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness, a tribute to the late rock singer. Authorized and supervised by Sharon and Jack Osbourn, this definitely is the love letter to the late singer that fans would expect. Filled with fan service, including a ride on the "Crazy Train," this walk through inspired by Ozzy's stage character ends with an intimate moment with the legend himself. This is another house that works for fans and those unfamiliar with the source IP.

But my pick for house of the year at 2026's Halloween Horror Nights is Universal's backstory set-up for this 35th anniversary event. Jack & Oddfellow: Chaos & Control tells how HHN icon Jack the Clown joined fellow icon Dr. Oddfellow's circus. But Jack's murder habit got in the way of Oddfellow's soul-stealing side hustle. When Oddfellow decided to off Jack (with a delicious pun as he does it), it all goes terribly wrong after Jack draws Oddfellow's enchanted blood while fighting back. That makes Jack immortal and sets up an eternal battle between the two.

Listen carefully for the "Pop Goes the Weasel" tune, which signals Jack's return. In the end, Jack and Oddfellow decide that fear divided is fear diluted and choose to join forces to create the Infernal Carnival of Nightmares - which just so happens to be the theme of this year's event. This house is a visual feast, filled with gags and treats to delight any HHN fan.

My second-favorite house this year was H.R. Bloodengutz Presents: A Halloween Fright-Tacular!, a callback to a decade-old original HHN house. This time, H.R. is out of prison and has taken over a TV station in HHN's favorite town of Carey, Ohio, to host a Halloween marathon of Universal Orlando made-up silly horror flicks that I would 100% percent watch in real life. Universal has produced plenty of anthology houses like this over the years. (Cinema Scare, anyone?) But every gag lands in this one, especially "The Madness of Dr. Pumpkinspyce," a mad scientist/barista who has infected millions. Watch the walk through video.

Other IP houses this year include Stranger Things 5, which leans into the series' monsters rather than deal with any of the emotional resolutions that frustrated so many fans about this Netflix's series final season. The demogorgons look better than ever here, and Vecna sets in a couple of jump scares. But the awe and wonder that this series inspires in its first go-around long has faded. Again, here is a video.

Universal's longest house this year is its tribute to Hellraiser, which is all fan service with its visual callbacks to the first three films. There's also Evil Dead Burn, a tribute to that franchise's most recent film, which delivers on its title's promise by turning up the heat - literally - in the house's final scenes.

This year's other original concept houses are Invasion: Alien Abduction, in also does exactly what its title says, with aliens abducting a family from their farm house. There are some nice gags in the farm house kitchen here, but your enjoyment of this one will correlate with your affinity for slasher aliens. Madlands: Caged Cannibals employs a punk metal soundtrack to envision a post-apocalyptic Old LA Zoo, where people continue to resist eating a vegetable even in a world where all animals are extinct, so they've turned to cannibalism. Just for the LOLs, they decide to cosplay extinct animals depicted in the ancient zoo's exhibits. All this provides an excuse for some impressively creative costuming.

Finally, Universal offers Cybergoria, a blood-splattered gore fest where the robots charged with figuring out to make human beings immortal just decide to thaw the cryogenic stiffs and flay them to access and plug into their nervous systems.

Gee, even in the year 3535, AI is gonna be making a mess of our lives. Talk about a horror night.

Thanks to Universal Orlando for inviting Theme Park Insider out again to cover the event.

title: Report: Universal Studios Japan plans major expansion
summary:
By Robert Niles: A news agency in Japan reports that Universal Studios Japan is planning a major expansion.

According to a report from Nikkei, Universal Destinations & Experiences is planning to spend up to US$1.8 billion to expand Universal Studios Japan onto nearly 15 acres of adjacent land owned by the city of Osaka.

Universal has not yet confirmed the plans, but Osaka's major has posted to social media that an announcement is coming next Thursday.

Like the Tokyo Disney theme parks, Universal Studios Japan is the final boss battle for global theme park fans. Visitors crowd the park nearly every day, with USJ drawing 16 million visitors in 2024, according to the latest TEA Global Experience Index attendance report. That makes USJ the world's third most popular park, behind Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom and California's Disneyland.

Unlike at those parks, USJ visitors almost all show up at rope drop and seem to hold PhDs in maximizing park time. That makes navigating the park a challenge for those who do not come prepared or do not buy a Universal Express pass. Clearly, there is demand for more attractions at the park.

Universal previously announced plans for a new Pokemon experience at Universal Studios Japan, with a version of that experience also expected to replace The Lost Continent at Universal Orlando's Islands of Adventure.
